mekan.ad: Topkapı'nın şehir içinden görünüşü ve önündeki meydan
mekan.tarif: The inner, city-side face of Topkapı, the great gate in the land walls of Constantinople, seen from inside the city at standing eye level about forty metres away, looking straight west into the gate. The massive round arch of pale limestone with bands of red brick fills the upper middle of the frame; its stones are cracked and scarred by cannon fire, and on the plastered inner face of the arch a large faded Byzantine fresco of a haloed figure in ochre and blue is half flaked away. Through the deep, shadowed passage of the arch the open sky beyond blazes white-gold. From the arch toward the camera runs a broad road of worn stone paving that opens into a wide square. A continuous cordon of janissaries in crimson kaftans and tall white felt börk caps stands shoulder to shoulder along both sides of the road, facing inward, holding tall plain crimson and green banners that each bear only a single white crescent. Behind the cordon, on heaps of fallen masonry, on the wall-walk above the gate, on the flat roofs and in the windows of the stone houses on both sides, thousands of townspeople stand packed and waiting: Greek men, women, old people, children on shoulders, in plain wool clothes of muted earth tones. The stone-paved centre of the road and the square is empty.
